input: Renovate my 1960s kitchen: new cabinets, countertops, flooring and lighting. I will hire a contractor for the electrical work and do the painting myself. Budget is not decided yet.

tasks.title: Read me first: assumptions and gaps
tasks.description:
This plan is a starting point and may still have gaps. Read the items below before relying on it.
The dates are suggestions meant to keep momentum. Moving one is normal, and overdue cards simply show in red.
Pacing assumed: about 10 hours a week, starting Mon 26 Oct (you did not say how much time you have). If you add your hours per week or a start date to the description and generate again, the dates will follow.
checklist: Assumption, verify: Permits are required for electrical work and possibly for other changes in a 1960s home How to check: Contact your local building or planning department and ask which permit types this renovation requires

Assumption, verify: The existing kitchen structure (walls, subfloor) is sound enough for new finishes without major structural repair How to check: Have a contractor or inspector assess the space before ordering materials

Assumption, verify: Asbestos or lead paint may be present in a 1960s home and must be tested before disturbing existing surfaces How to check: Hire a certified inspector or buy a test kit; check local regulations for disposal rules
Assumption, verify: Standard cabinet sizes will fit the existing layout without moving walls or plumbing How to check: Measure carefully and confirm with your cabinet supplier before ordering

Assumption, verify: The electrical panel has enough capacity for any new lighting circuits the contractor recommends How to check: Ask the electrical contractor to assess the panel during their quote visit
On "Assess existing kitchen and check for hazardous materials": If tests come back positive, check with a professional and your local authority before proceeding.
On "Request permits from local building department": Assumption, verify: permit approval time in your area.
On "Get quotes from contractors and suppliers": Assumption, verify: cabinet lead times in your area, as semi-custom or custom cabinets can take several weeks.
On "Order cabinets and await delivery": Assumption, verify: actual lead time with your chosen supplier.
For any price, rate or rule above: check the vendor or official source directly, or ask a professional for anything legal or financial.
tasks.notes:
NOT MENTIONED IN YOUR DESCRIPTION (often matters):
- Appliance replacement or keeping existing appliances is not mentioned
- Plumbing changes (sink, faucet, dishwasher) are not addressed
- Backsplash is not mentioned
- Disposal or storage of old cabinets and materials is not planned
- Whether anyone else (partner, landlord, HOA) needs to approve the renovation is not mentioned

THINGS THIS PLAN CANNOT KNOW:
- Current cost of cabinets, countertops, and flooring materials in your area
- Contractor availability and lead times in your area
- What permits cost locally and how long approval takes
- Whether hazardous materials (asbestos, lead) are present and what removal costs

POSSIBLE CONFLICTS TO CHECK:
- "Get quotes from contractors and suppliers" rests on an unchecked assumption but its first step is not a check.

tasks.title: Decisions needed: choices only you can make
tasks.description: These choices were not in your description, so they are yours to make. Each has a recommended default: accept it and move on, or swap it for your own.
checklist: What is the overall budget for this renovation? Options: Set a firm ceiling before getting quotes / Collect quotes first, then set a budget based on what you learn. Recommended default: Collect quotes first, then set a budget based on what you learn.

Which cabinet style and material do you want (stock, semi-custom, or custom)? Options: Stock cabinets (fastest, least expensive) / Semi-custom cabinets (more choice, moderate lead time) / Custom cabinets (most flexibility, longest lead time). Recommended default: Semi-custom cabinets (more choice, moderate lead time).
Which countertop material do you want? Options: Laminate / Quartz / Granite / Butcher block. Recommended default: Quartz.
Which flooring material do you want? Options: Luxury vinyl plank / Ceramic or porcelain tile / Hardwood. Recommended default: Luxury vinyl plank.
Will you replace the sink and faucet at the same time? Options: Yes / No. Recommended default: Yes, since cabinets will be removed anyway.

tasks.title: Assess existing kitchen and check for hazardous materials
tasks.description:
Inspect the current kitchen thoroughly and test for asbestos or lead paint before disturbing any surfaces, as both were common in 1960s homes.
Why this matters: Finding hazards early prevents costly surprises and keeps the project legally and safely on track.
checklist: Photograph and measure the full kitchen, noting all walls, windows, and outlets
Buy or hire a certified test for asbestos (floor tiles, ceiling) and lead paint
Note condition of walls and subfloor for the contractor's assessment
List all items to be removed: cabinets, countertops, flooring, light fixtures
tasks.notes: Asbestos and lead were common in homes built before the 1980s. If tests come back positive, check with a professional and your local authority before proceeding. Do not sand or cut suspect materials until cleared.

tasks.title: Make key material and scope decisions
tasks.description:
Depends on: Assess existing kitchen and check for hazardous materials
Decide on cabinet style, countertop, flooring, and whether the sink and faucet will be replaced, so you can get accurate quotes.
Why this matters: Contractors and suppliers cannot give firm quotes without knowing what you want.
checklist: Choose cabinet style (stock, semi-custom, or custom) from the decisions list
Choose countertop material from the decisions list
Choose flooring material from the decisions list
Decide whether to replace the sink and faucet
Note preferred lighting style (under-cabinet, recessed, pendant, etc.)
tasks.notes: These decisions feed directly into quotes. Changing them after ordering can cause delays and restocking fees.

tasks.title: Get quotes from contractors and suppliers
tasks.description:
Depends on: Make key material and scope decisions
Collect at least three quotes for electrical work, cabinet installation, countertop fabrication, and flooring, using the decisions made in the earlier card.
Why this matters: Quotes give you real numbers to set a budget and choose reliable tradespeople.
checklist: Contact at least three licensed electricians for a quote on new lighting circuits and fixtures
Get quotes from at least two cabinet suppliers based on your chosen style
Get a quote from at least one countertop fabricator (measure twice before ordering)
Get quotes from at least two flooring suppliers or installers
Ask each contractor for references and proof of license and insurance
Ask about lead times for materials, especially cabinets
tasks.notes: Assumption, verify: cabinet lead times in your area, as semi-custom or custom cabinets can take several weeks. Factor this into your schedule.

tasks.title: Decision: Set budget and select contractors
tasks.description:
Depends on: Get quotes from contractors and suppliers
Review all quotes, set your renovation budget, and choose which contractors and suppliers to hire.
Why this matters: No work should be ordered or started until budget and contractors are confirmed.
checklist: Compare all quotes and confirm you are comfortable with the total cost
Set your overall budget ceiling
Select and notify chosen contractors and suppliers
Confirm start dates and material delivery windows with each party
Sign contracts and pay any required deposits

tasks.title: Request permits from local building department
tasks.description:
Depends on: Make key material and scope decisions
Apply for any permits required for electrical work and other changes, as a 1960s renovation commonly triggers permit requirements.
Why this matters: Work done without required permits can result in fines and problems when selling the home.
checklist: Contact local building department to confirm which permits are needed
Submit permit applications for electrical work (and any others required)
Pay permit fees and note inspection requirements
Keep permit documents on site once approved
tasks.notes: Assumption, verify: permit approval time in your area. Timelines vary widely by municipality.

tasks.title: Demolish existing kitchen surfaces
tasks.description:
Depends on: Decision: Set budget and select contractors; Request permits from local building department
Remove old cabinets, countertops, flooring, and light fixtures to prepare the space for new work.
Why this matters: Everything else depends on a cleared and prepared kitchen space.
checklist: Confirm hazardous material results are clear before cutting or sanding anything
Turn off electricity to the kitchen at the breaker before removing fixtures
Remove light fixtures, then cabinets, then countertops, then flooring
Inspect subfloor and wall surfaces once stripped; note any damage
Arrange disposal or donation of removed materials
Protect adjacent rooms from dust with plastic sheeting
tasks.notes: Check with your local authority or a professional if any hazardous materials were found in "Assess existing kitchen and check for hazardous materials" before doing any demolition. Subfloor: the structural layer of floor beneath the finished flooring.

tasks.title: Repair walls and subfloor as needed
tasks.description:
Depends on: Demolish existing kitchen surfaces
Fix any damage to walls or the subfloor uncovered during demolition before installing new materials.
Why this matters: New cabinets, flooring, and finishes need a sound, level surface to look good and last.
checklist: Patch holes or damaged drywall and let compound dry fully before painting
Check subfloor for soft spots, squeaks, or unevenness and repair
Confirm walls are plumb and floor is level enough for new cabinets and flooring
Consult a professional if structural damage is found
tasks.notes: Drywall compound (also called joint compound or mud) needs time to dry before sanding or painting. Allow at least 24 hours per coat.

tasks.title: Complete electrical rough-in and new circuits
tasks.description:
Depends on: Repair walls and subfloor as needed; Request permits from local building department
Have the licensed electrical contractor run any new wiring needed for lighting circuits before walls are closed up or cabinets installed.
Why this matters: Wiring must be in place before cabinets go up, and inspected before walls are closed.
checklist: Coordinate contractor start date to follow wall and subfloor repairs
Contractor runs new wiring for lighting and any additional circuits
Schedule and pass required rough-in electrical inspection
Confirm locations of switches and fixtures match the lighting plan
tasks.notes: Rough-in: the stage where wiring is run inside walls before they are closed. Inspections at this stage are often required before you can continue.

tasks.title: Order cabinets and await delivery
tasks.description:
Depends on: Decision: Set budget and select contractors
Place the cabinet order as soon as contractors are selected, since cabinets are typically the longest lead-time item.
Why this matters: Delays in cabinet delivery will push back the entire installation sequence.
checklist: Confirm final measurements with the supplier before placing the order
Place the order and get a written delivery date
Arrange a delivery location that keeps cabinets safe and dry
tasks.notes: Assumption, verify: actual lead time with your chosen supplier. Stock cabinets arrive faster than semi-custom or custom.

tasks.title: Paint walls and ceiling
tasks.description:
Depends on: Repair walls and subfloor as needed; Complete electrical rough-in and new circuits
Paint the kitchen walls and ceiling yourself before cabinets and flooring go in, which is much easier than painting around finished work.
Why this matters: Painting before installation saves significant time and produces a cleaner result.
checklist: Choose paint color and finish (semi-gloss or satin is typical for kitchens)
Prime bare or patched drywall before applying finish coats
Apply at least two finish coats, allowing drying time between coats
Paint ceiling first, then walls
Mask off any electrical boxes or surfaces not being painted
tasks.notes: Semi-gloss and satin finishes are easier to clean than flat paint, which matters in a kitchen.

tasks.title: Install new flooring
tasks.description:
Depends on: Repair walls and subfloor as needed; Order cabinets and await delivery
Lay the new kitchen floor after painting and electrical rough-in are complete but before cabinets go in (or follow your flooring installer's recommendation on sequence).
Why this matters: Flooring sequence affects how cabinets sit and how the finished floor looks at the edges.
checklist: Confirm with your flooring supplier whether to install before or after cabinets
Allow flooring material to acclimate in the room per manufacturer instructions
Install flooring starting from the most visible area of the room
Install transition strips at doorways
Inspect finished floor for gaps or loose areas before proceeding
tasks.notes: Acclimation: letting flooring material sit in the room for a period so it adjusts to the temperature and humidity before installation. This reduces buckling or gapping later.

tasks.title: Install new cabinets
tasks.description:
Depends on: Paint walls and ceiling; Order cabinets and await delivery; Install new flooring
Install upper and lower cabinets once painting is done, flooring sequence is confirmed, and cabinets have been delivered.
Why this matters: Cabinets are the largest installation step and set the layout for everything that follows.
checklist: Verify all cabinet boxes and doors were delivered undamaged
Find and mark wall studs for secure mounting
Install upper cabinets before lower cabinets to avoid working over base units
Check each cabinet for level and plumb before fastening fully
Install cabinet doors and hardware after boxes are secured
Leave space for the countertop template if countertop is fabricated to measure
tasks.notes: Plumb: perfectly vertical. Level: perfectly horizontal. Both matter for doors to hang and close properly.

tasks.title: Complete electrical finish work and install light fixtures
tasks.description:
Depends on: Install new cabinets; Complete electrical rough-in and new circuits
Have the electrical contractor return to install light fixtures and connect switches now that cabinets and surfaces are in place.
Why this matters: Finish electrical work cannot be done until the surfaces it mounts to are in place.
checklist: Confirm fixture types and locations with the contractor before the visit
Contractor installs light fixtures and switch plates
Schedule and pass any required final electrical inspection
Test all lights and switches before signing off

tasks.title: Template and install countertops
tasks.description:
Depends on: Install new cabinets
Have the countertop fabricator measure (template) the installed cabinets, then fabricate and install the countertop.
Why this matters: Countertops must be measured after cabinets are in place to fit correctly.
checklist: Schedule the fabricator to come and template the installed cabinets
Confirm sink cutout location and any special edge profiles during the template visit
Allow fabrication lead time before installation appointment
Inspect countertop on delivery for chips, cracks, or wrong dimensions
Have fabricator install and seal countertop
tasks.notes: Template: a precise pattern made from your cabinets that the fabricator uses to cut the countertop to the exact shape. This step cannot happen until cabinets are in. waitDays covers typical fabrication time; verify with your supplier.

tasks.title: Paint touch-ups and finishing details
tasks.description:
Depends on: Template and install countertops; Complete electrical finish work and install light fixtures
Do a final round of painting touch-ups and install any remaining hardware, trim, or accessories.
Why this matters: Small finishing details are what make a renovation look complete and professional.
checklist: Touch up paint anywhere scuffed during installation
Install cabinet knobs and pulls if not already done
Install any trim or molding around cabinets or flooring edges
Caulk gaps between countertop, backsplash area, and wall

tasks.title: Final inspection and project close-out
tasks.description:
Depends on: Paint touch-ups and finishing details
Do a full walkthrough to confirm everything meets your expectations and that all required inspections have been passed.
Why this matters: Closing out properly ensures permits are signed off and problems are caught while contractors are still reachable.
checklist: Confirm all required permit inspections are completed and signed off
Walk through with each contractor to review their work and raise any deficiencies
Collect all warranties, manuals, and receipts for materials and appliances
Photograph the finished kitchen for your records

Get quotes from contractors and suppliers
Decision: Set budget and select contractors
